maria: quick question — which of these is the change that touched KV cache warmup?
jon: looks like 1a2b3c4d5e (nate) — runtime patch. nate's PR description mentions "kv cache prefetch for long-tail"
lee: tagging @sre-bot for perf watch on canary (latency) :eyes:
sre-bot: canary deployed to subset: prod-canary-3 (10% traffic). health checks passing (4/4) — latency +0.8% so far
maria: can we pin platform @release-2026.03.1 for the rest of the rollout? that platform commit includes a config tweak we want consistent in prod
jon: i can pin. proposed plan: pin platform at 8f5d2a3f4b and continue rollout for runtime/console. if canary degrades, rollback runtime to previous sha 7e6f5a4
maria: ack, please add rollback note to release thread and notify support. also add the commit authors to the release notes (carol, nate, priya)
jon: done — added short blurb to release notes: "Fix: KV cache warmup (nate). Ops: platform config stabilization (carol). UX: console error visibility (priya)." link: https://confluence.redwood.dev/releases/2026-03-1
deploybot: [prod][us-east-1] batch #7 APPLY complete — 3 commits — batch runtime id: r-2026031423
sre-bot: brief perf snapshot (canary window 300s): p50=42ms (+0.8%), p95=180ms (+1.2%). no error rate spike. continuing monitoring for 10m
lee: if p95 crosses +5% we flip to rollback plan A (runtime rollback to 7e6f5a4)
maria: noted. leaving final decision to @oncall (if they request rollback, we execute). tagging paging policy in the release thread
jon: heads-up — I'll open the rollback PR if needed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/419 (draft)
deploybot: [prod][us-east-1] rollout FINISHED for batch #7 — status: SUCCESS — commits: 8f5d2a3f4b, 1a2b3c4d5e, d4c3b2a1f0 — authors: carol, nate, priya — details: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/98765
maria: thanks all. will finalize release notes and ping growth for post-release announcement :tada:
jon: added commit author attributions to the changelog and included PR links in the CI artifact
lee: one last check — minimal smoke command I ran: ```kubectl get pods -n prod | grep runtime | awk '{print $2" "$4}'``` all runtime pods: 1/1 Ready
jon: closing thread. filing follow-up ticket to validate kv warmup behavior across long sessions: RED-3421
